full_judgment:
5. Mr. Subrata Saha, the learned advocate appearing for the petitioner in support of the rule mainly took us to the ground taken in the application to the effect that in order to make a person liable under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument (Amendment) Act,1994, the payee of the cheque has to give a notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque within 15 days of the receipt of information by him from the Bank concerned regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid in terms of clause (b) to the proviso and in the instant case the cheque was lastly been dishonoured on 26.1.2000 and the complaint issued notice upon the petitioner on 28.2.2000 after 18 days of statutory period of limitation and as such the mandatory provision of clause (b) of the proviso to section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument has not been complied with and as such the initiation and continuation of the impugned proceeding clearly amounts to an abuse of process of the court and the same is liable to be quashed in the interest of justice. In support of his contention the learned advocate cited a decision in the case of S.M. Anwar Hossain-Vs- Md. Shafiqul Alam (Chand) and another reported in 19 BLD (AD),166. 

 8. In this case rule was obtained to quash the proceeding mainly on the ground that the complainant issued a legal notice upon the accused petitioner after expiry of the statutory period of limitation as provided under section 138 (b) of the Negotiable Instrument Act. In order to appreciate the argument advanced by the parties, we like to see the relevant provision of law. 

 15. Now in this case it appears that the alleged cheque lastly been dishonoured on 26.1.2000 and in that view of the above legal position a notice for demanding money is required to give absolutely on or before 10.2.2000( within 15 days of the receipt of the information) but in the instant case, a notice upon the complainant was issued as per the petition of complaint, on 28.2.2000 long after the statutory period of limitation and as such the mandatory provision, of issuance of notice under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act has not been complied with, the case apparently was filed after the limitation as framed by the legislature, accordingly the case is barred by law and the impugned criminal proceeding in its present form is an abuse of the process of the Court and is thus liable to be quashed. 

 16. We have gone through the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, namely in the case of Faridul Alam -Vs- The State and another reported in 27 BLD (AD)140. The point raised in this matter regarding the question of limitation has neither been placed nor been considered in the said case. The word "refer to drawer" as remarked by the bank as well as plea of the accused has been agitated and decided therein and in the case of Satya Narayan Podder Vs- State and another reported in 53 DLR,403, the Hon'ble High Court Division has considered the question of prematurity of the case. In the said case, the case was filed before the expiry of 15 days and their lordships on holding that even after expiry of the 15 days, since the accused person did not take any step to repay the money, in course of time the cause of action although was premature but during the proceeding the defect has been cured. We thus found that the above cited decisions placed by the learned advocate for the opposite party has got no manner of its application in the instant case. However since we have found above that institution of the instant criminal proceedings was not in complying with the time limit, it is barred by limitation, the impugned criminal proceeding is thus liable to be quashed. We find merit in this rule.
